title: Did You Know a Giant Ice Cream Scoop Weighed More Than a Car?
summary:
Imagine a scoop of ice cream so huge it weighs more than a car! In 2014, workers in Wisconsin made the world's biggest single scoop. They poured 733 tubs of ice cream into a giant freezer box, then snow sculptors carved it into a perfect scoop. It stood over five feet tall and weighed 3,010 pounds. That's like stacking 10 big kids on a scale! After the record was confirmed, everyone at the festival got to eat it.

July is National Ice Cream Month in the United States. President Ronald Reagan started this sweet tradition in 1984. He also made the third Sunday of July National Ice Cream Day. So, you have a whole month to enjoy your favorite frozen treat!

Ice cream has a long history. The first ice-cream-like dessert was made in China over 1,000 years ago, with milk, flour, and camphor. A more modern version came from Arab chefs in the 9th century. It arrived in America in 1744, when a governor served strawberry ice cream at a party. George Washington loved it so much he spent about $200 in one summer—a huge amount back then. Thomas Jefferson even wrote a vanilla ice cream recipe.

Today, the average American eats about 23 pounds of ice cream every year. That's like carrying around a big bag of dog food made of ice cream! California makes the most ice cream, but the biggest fans live in Rhode Island, Wisconsin, and Washington, D.C.

Did you know your favorite flavor might say something about you? A scientist found that vanilla lovers are often adventurous. Chocolate fans are outgoing and energetic. Strawberry pickers are thoughtful and loyal. Mint chocolate chip people are ambitious and confident. So, what's your scoop say about you?
why_it_matters: Ice cream is a fun treat, and learning about its history and record-breaking versions can make you appreciate how something simple can bring people together at a festival or on a hot summer day.
